chapter: Bands and musicians around New Orleans
title: Jimmy Noon, Bechet and the borrowed clarinet
summary: Noon playing in the district, friendship with Bechet, and the story of Bechet finding and repairing an old clarinet at Bay St. Louis.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Sure. No, I know him when he was around here. When he first went around here trying to play around here. He was playing George Fewclothes on Franklin and, uh, me and Franklin and Neighborville, which used to be Franklin and Custom House. Mm-hmm. Right across from 25. George Fewclothes.
Oh, yeah.
That way he was playing in there.
Was he any good there?
He was coming up.
He was coming up young.
He was coming up young, yeah.
Off the plantation, right?

And that way, uh, Bassier used to come in there and, uh, Jimbo, let Bassier play, you know. Them fellas down in the district, a fella come and complain if they, they leave you there on the job and they go on off, you know.
Mm-hmm.
Run around, go anywhere they want. You know that guy gonna stay there and play until you come back.
Yeah.
Some of them used to go off and wouldn't come back.
Well, how did Bassier and Noon compare? Did they ever bop there? Would they ever have a contest?
Bassier and Jimmy?
Yeah. No, they didn't have no cotton. They were friends, huh?

They were friends. Bassier, this guy went there and blowed. And could blow. We was over in Bass St. Louis with Madeline and guitar. Bass. And Bassier was sitting out there on the trunces, you know. And we happened to come out. And that's what he was doing there, he said. Suck down, he just come on over on excursion. So, he said, got your clint in? He said, no, I ain't got no horn. So, there was an old man there. He said, what did he play? I said, he plays a clint in. Know anybody around here that got a clint in? He said, let me see. He said, oh, I think there's one back there in the loft up there in the barn. He said, that thing's been back there for years. Bassier said, go get it. He said, I don't think you can do anything with it. I said, go get it. You can't never tell. You know what I mean? I went and got him brushed the cobwebs out of it. It was just as dusty. And it was a key. Shark broke.
Mm-hmm.

It was a long time. And a reed. You know what I mean? A reed. And in this man's backyard, they grew this, those, what you call them, trees, you know, the reed. Bamboo. Bam, yeah. He went back there and he cut him a stalk off about that long. And come back and sit out there on the track where the welling man used to run. And cut him out a couple of reeds. Now, he's got to fix them all. Key. Did you know he missed around there? Called him out of key. And put on that old clarinet.
Mm-hmm.
In there, he got a tone out. It was so dry, anyway. He poured a bowl of water in it, you know. He sat down there and played that clarinet all day. And I played the devil out of it.
